definitions.explanation: A young sheep. Used both for the live animal and for lamb meat in cooking contexts.

examples.japanese: {子羊|こひつじ}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{生|う}まれた→生まれる：00905_umareru⟧。
⟦{牧場|ぼくじょう}→牧場：06103_bokujou⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧{子羊|こひつじ}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{触|さわ}れる→触る：00808_sawaru⟧。
examples.english: You can pet lambs at the farm.

examples.japanese: {子羊|こひつじ}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{肉|にく}→肉：02240_niku⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧やわらかくて{臭|くさ}み⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{少|すく}ない→少ない：01136_sukunai⟧。
examples.english: Lamb meat is tender and has less of a gamey smell.

notes:
Composed of ⟦{子|こ}→子：09851_ko⟧ (young, offspring) + ⟦{羊|ひつじ}→羊：04713_hitsuji⟧ (sheep). Refers to a young sheep, typically under one year old. Also used as a food term for lamb meat, though ラム is more common in restaurant menus.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {子羊|こひつじ}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{肉|にく}→肉：02240_niku⟧: lamb meat
- ⟦{迷|まよ}え→迷う：02426_mayou⟧る{子羊|こひつじ}: a lost lamb (figuratively, someone who is lost or confused)
- {子羊|こひつじ}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧ロースト: roast lamb

CULTURAL NOTE:
The phrase ⟦{迷|まよ}え→迷う：02426_mayou⟧る{子羊|こひつじ} (lost lamb) comes from Christian scripture and is used figuratively in Japanese to describe someone who is troubled, lost, or seeking guidance. It is widely understood even among non-Christians.

RELATED WORDS:
- ⟦{羊|ひつじ}→羊：04713_hitsuji⟧: sheep (adult)
- ラム: lamb (as a meat term, from English)
